Below is a comprehensive ‟pytest style” test-suite for `hex_to_rgb`.  
It checks normal behaviour, boundary/edge cases and a variety of failure modes.

Save it as `test_hex_to_rgb.py` (adjust the import so it points to the file
that contains `hex_to_rgb`).

```python
import pytest

# Replace `your_module` with the actual module name that hosts hex_to_rgb
from your_module import hex_to_rgb


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Happy-path / nominal-case tests
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "raw_hex, expected",
    [
        ("#FFA07A", (255, 160, 122)),  # canonical ‟#RRGGBB”
        ("FFA07A",  (255, 160, 122)),  # without the leading '#'
        ("#000000", (0, 0, 0)),        # all zeros
        ("#FFFFFF", (255, 255, 255)),  # all max
        ("#abcdef", (171, 205, 239)),  # lower-case letters
        ("ABCDEF",  (171, 205, 239)),  # upper-case, no '#'
        ("#11223344",  (17, 34, 51)),  # 8-digit string, alpha channel ignored
    ],
)
def test_hex_to_rgb_happy_path(raw_hex, expected):
    assert hex_to_rgb(raw_hex) == expected


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Edge & boundary cases that should raise a ValueError
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad_hex",
    [
        "",           # empty string
        "#",          # only the '#'
        "#123",       # 3-digit shorthand not supported by implementation
        "123",        # ditto, without '#'
        "#FFFFF",     # 5 characters
        "#12345",     # 5 characters again – off by one
        "#1234567",   # 7 characters
        "GGHHII",     # non-hex digits
        "#ZZZZZZ",    # non-hex digits with '#'
        "  FFA07A",   # leading whitespace not stripped
    ],
)
def test_hex_to_rgb_invalid_valueerror(bad_hex):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        hex_to_rgb(bad_hex)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Non-string inputs – implementation attempts .lstrip(), so
# AttributeError is expected.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
@pytest.mark.parametrize("non_string", [None, 123, 12.34, ["#FFA07A"], b"#FFA07A"])
def test_hex_to_rgb_non_string_inputs(non_string):
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
        hex_to_rgb(non_string)
```

Explanation of coverage
• Happy path – verifies correct tuples for multiple valid representations, different
  letter-cases and the “8-digit” edge where the last two characters are silently ignored.

• Edge cases – strings of wrong length, shorthand 3-digit form, illegal characters,
  leading whitespace etc.  All of these eventually cause `int(<bad>, 16)` to raise
  `ValueError`, which we assert.

• Error cases – non-string arguments trigger `AttributeError` because `.lstrip('#')`
  cannot be called.  These inputs validate type-robustness.

Run the test-suite with `pytest -q` and it should report all tests passing for a
correct implementation.
